overview: Both are blood vessels, but capillaries are the tiny exchange sites while arteries are the larger transport pipes leading to them.
genZNote: Artery: the highway. Capillary: the narrow driveway where the actual delivery happens.

aspects.label: Size / Diameter
aspects.valueA: Relatively large diameter, thick muscular walls.

aspects.label: Function
aspects.valueA: Transports blood at high pressure away from the heart to organs.
aspects.valueB: Site of actual exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste between blood and tissues.

aspects.label: Wall Structure
aspects.valueA: Three layers: tunica intima, media, and externa.
aspects.valueB: A single layer of endothelial cells, allowing diffusion.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Capillaries are the only blood vessels thin enough for gas and nutrient exchange to actually occur across their walls.
overlay.memoryTrick: Capillary walls are just one cell thick — built for exchange, not transport.
overlay.commonMisconception: Blood does not exchange gases/nutrients across artery or vein walls — that exchange happens exclusively at the capillary level.
